learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the invisible ways heat travels through solids, liquids, and empty space to keep our world warm and moving!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: When you leave a metal spoon in a hot bowl of soup, the handle gets warm! This happens through conduction. Heat energy passes from one tiny particle to the next, just like a line of falling dominoes, usually in solid objects.

Liquids and gases transfer heat by actually moving around! When water boils, the hot water at the bottom rises to the top, and the cooler water sinks to get heated. This continuous circular dance is called convection.

How does the warmth of the Sun reach Earth through empty, freezing space? It uses radiation! This type of heat transfer does not need any particles or materials to travel through; it moves as invisible waves of energy.

fun_activity.title: 🧊 The Great Ice Melting Race
fun_activity.instructions: Place one ice cube on a metal plate and another on a plastic or wooden plate. Watch closely to see which one melts faster and discover which material is a better conductor of heat!

quick_recap: ⭐ Heat always flows from a hotter object to a colder object until both reach the same temperature.
⭐ Conduction happens in touching solids, while convection creates currents in liquids and gases.
⭐ Radiation allows heat energy to travel through empty space without needing a medium.
